sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r12/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (openpyxl read_only, in memory): 'Quality Checks' row 25 (#24 grading_wiring_is_structurally_correct), 'Internal Quality Checks' row 25 (legacy wording: reward.toml, pinned judge, valid aggregate), 'Deterministic Checks' rows check-rubric-schema.py, check-scoring-policy.py, check-required-files.py; no comment parts in the xlsx zip
evidence: Parsed every file with Python tomllib from scratchpad (no workspace writes). scoring.toml (lines 1-11): [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2 (sum 1.0); [floors] functional=0.05; byte-identical to the frozen template (diff SAME); each name has its directory (tests/gates/{render,constraints}, tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}). All five judge.toml exist in the right suite, LF only, top-level keys exactly judge/scoring/criterion. Each [judge] = {judge='claude-code' (matches task.toml REWARDKIT_JUDGE line 31), mode='batched', timeout, isolated=false, prompt_template='prompt.md'} with no model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight. Timeouts: render 600, constraints 600, functional 9000, polish 900, visual 900 (same as template); gates 1200 < test.sh run_suite gates 1500 (test.sh:213), scored 10800 < 11100 (test.sh:224), 1500+11100=12600 < verifier 13200 (task.toml:27). Every judge.toml declares the playwright MCP server (command playwright-mcp, args --headless --isolated --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium --no-sandbox). Only scored/functional/judge.toml:14-18 declares name='verifier', command='/usr/local/bin/python3', args=['/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py', '$APP_RESTART_HELPER'], matching test.sh:193 'export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh"'; test.sh, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/Dockerfile and .dockerignore are byte-identical to the template. Functional prompt uses restart_app once (prompt.md:1, :51) and forbids shell. [scoring] aggregation: gates all_pass, scored weighted_mean. Criteria: render 1 (hro_gate_render, binary, w1.0), constraints 1 (hro_gate_shared, binary, w1.0) -> gates binary-only; functional 44 binary, weights 0.5-2.5 all positive, ids unique; polish 5 binary (w 3,3,2,1.5,2.5) unique; visual 5 likert points=5 w1.2 each, each description carries 5..1 anchors (visual/judge.toml:20-31). Every criterion has id, name, type, weight, non-empty description; no extra keys. Prompts resolve: each prompt_template file exists, contains {criteria} and {app_context}, opens http://localhost:3000; no other brace placeholders or stray braces in any prompt or in app_context.md (grep empty), so test.sh:198-200 substitution and RewardKit {criteria} formatting cannot trip. Workbook-vs-internal note: Internal sheet row 24 still describes the retired layout (reward.toml, 'pinned judge'); current Quality Checks wording and SKILL delivery profile (model in judge.toml is a defect) govern, so absence of a pinned model is correct. Counterexample probes: a dead/static app cannot exploit wiring because gates are all_pass binary at 0.0 and score.py (template-identical) zeroes on gate failure and applies the functional floor; a conforming app is not failed by wiring because the restart helper variable, MCP servers and placeholders are those of the canonical template. Minor non-structural note: scored/polish/prompt.md:12 reads 'gives binary0 throughout' (missing space) - harmless wording, not a wiring defect. Evidence limits: static parse/diff only. raw-evidence-index.json states full configured grading is absent, so RewardKit actually loading these five judge.toml files and expanding $APP_RESTART_HELPER in this candidate is Not exercised; risk left false because every structural element is either template-identical or statically verified, and missing configured-run evidence belongs to the workload/runtime rows, not waived here.
